stories.title: Wiki search ignores the article key

agent.summary: Fixed searchWiki in the support-studio capsule so that a ticket text mentioning an article's key (api, login, billing, integration, bug) adds 2 extra points to that article's score even when none of its keywords match; changed score to let and applied score += 2. Added a test verifying the key-only bonus and confirmed text matching nothing still returns { found: false }.

turns.assistantText: The bug is in `searchWiki`: the key-bonus line `if (lower.includes(key)) score + 2` computes a value but never assigns it. Also `score` is `const`, so it can't be reassigned. Let me fix it:
Now let me add tests covering the new behavior:
Now let me run the tests and the gatekeeper:
Both checks pass. Let me verify the final state of the fix:

The fix is complete and verified.

## Summary

In `plugins/support-studio/lib/support-core.js`, `searchWiki` had the key-mention bonus line `if (lower.includes(key)) score + 2` which computed a value but never assigned it — and `score` was declared `const`, so it couldn't be reassigned either. 

**Change:**
- Changed `score` to `let` and added the bonus with `score += 2` when the ticket text contains the article's key. This applies even when none of the article's keywords match (e.g. "please fix the api" now finds the `api` article).
- The `bestScore > 0` guard is untouched, so text matching nothing still returns `{ found: false }`.

**Tests:**
- Added a test in `plugins/support-studio/test/support.test.js` verifying that text containing only an article key (no keyword matches) scores the +2 bonus and finds the article.

All 143 tests pass and the contract gatekeeper reports **FAST_TRACK** (merge-ready, strict capsule-internal change, no contract mutation).

stories.title: Wiki article generation crashes on a matching ticket

agent.summary: Fixed generateWikiArticle(input) throwing on string inputs that match a knowledge-base article by looking up the article via searchWiki(input) instead of the draft reply, and added tests for the matched and unmatched string cases.

turns.assistantText: The tests pass. Now I understand the code. In `generateWikiArticle`'s string branch, it uses `r.wiki.article`, but `draftReply` only returns `{ found, key }` in its `wiki` field — not the `article` — so accessing `r.wiki.article.title` throws a TypeError when a match is found. Let me fix it by using `searchWiki` directly to obtain the article.
Now let me add tests for the string branch: one for a matching article and one for the no-match case.

Both the full test suite (145 passing, including the 2 new tests) and the contract gatekeeper pass. The bug was that `generateWikiArticle(input)` for a string input relied on `draftReply`'s `wiki` field, which only carries `{ found, key }` — not the article object — so accessing `r.wiki.article.title` threw when a knowledge-base article matched. I fixed it by calling `searchWiki(input)` directly in the string branch to obtain the matched article.

Summary of changes:
- **`plugins/support-studio/lib/support-core.js`**: In `generateWikiArticle`, the string branch now looks up the matched article via `searchWiki(input)` (falling back to `draftReply` only for classification/id/tags). A matching string yields a Markdown article titled `<article title> (resolved)`, with the article's title as root cause and its body as resolution; a non-matching string keeps the existing `New issue resolved` output.
- **`plugins/support-studio/test/support.test.js`**: Added tests covering both the matched-article string case and the no-match case.

stories.title: Spanish urgency terms in ticket classification

agent.summary: In the support-studio capsule, `classifyTicket(text)` now understands Spanish: `urgente`, `caído`/`caido`, and `bloqueado` map to `high` urgency, and `no funciona` counts as a `bug` category keyword. English behavior is unchanged, and tests plus the contract gatekeeper all pass.

turns.assistantText: Now I understand the structure. Let me look at how the classification logic works and make the changes to `classifyTicket`.
Now let me add tests for the Spanish behavior next to the existing classification tests.

I realized there's a subtlety: JavaScript's `\b` is ASCII-based, so `\bcaído\b` won't match because `ó` isn't a word character. Let me verify and fix by using `caí?do` which keeps the word boundary on the ASCII `o`, handling both spellings.
Let me check the local test runner and run the tests.
The regex `caí?do` doesn't match `caido` (plain `i`) — it only matches `cado`/`caído`. I need `ca[ií]do` to allow either `i` or `í`.
The regex ends at ASCII `o`, so the trailing `\b` works, and the leading `\b` before `c` also works. Now let me re-run the tests.
All 169 tests pass. Now let me run the gatekeeper.

Both the test suite and the contract gatekeeper pass. The change is complete.

## Summary

In `plugins/support-studio/lib/support-core.js` (the customer-support module):

1. **Urgency**: `classifyTicket(text)` now treats the Spanish words `urgente`, `caído`/`caido`, and `bloqueado` as `high` urgency. The regex uses `ca[ií]do` so word boundaries work around the accented characters while accepting both spellings.

2. **Bug category**: the phrase `no funciona` was added to the `bug` category keywords, so it counts toward the `bug` category score.

English behavior is unchanged — all existing English keywords, urgency words, and categorization logic remain exactly as before.

I also added tests next to the existing ones in `plugins/support-studio/test/support.test.js` covering: `urgente` → high, `caído` → high, `caido` (no accent) → high, `bloqueado` → high, and `no funciona` → `bug` category (without inadvertently raising urgency).

## Summary

I modified `plugins/spec-parser/lib/spec.js` so that when `parseRequirement` receives free text, a gain given in decibels (a number followed by `dB` right after the gain keyword, e.g. `ganancia de 40 dB` or `gain 20 dB`) is converted to its linear V/V value using `10^(dB/20)`.

### Changes

1. **`findGain` in `plugins/spec-parser/lib/spec.js`**:
   - Added a `decibelsToLinear(db)` helper that computes `10^(db/20)`.
   - The gain-keyword pattern (`ganancia`/`gain`) now optionally captures a trailing `dB` suffix; when present, the nominal gain is stored as the linear value (`40 dB` → `100`, `20 dB` → `10`).
